prerequisites: Basic Operations (Basic Operations I) for Industrial Chemical Engineering students

learning_outcomes.text: Understand and master basic concepts about the different pollutants emitted in human and industrial activities and their effects on the Environment.
Ability to identify the different preventive and corrective instruments that can be used in environmental management.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply environmental legislation.
Knowledge of existing methodologies for pollution prevention and control.
Identify environmental aspects of different industrial activities, selecting the most significant ones.
Identify legal requirements regarding pollution prevention and control.
Manage preventive and corrective environmental management instruments: environmental impact assessment, environmental management systems, environmental audits.
Propose methodologies for the treatment, valorization and elimination of effluents and waste.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the environment and sustainable development
Dispersion of pollutants in the atmosphere
Control technologies for gaseous pollutant removal
Effects of pollutants on water. Discharge regulations
Physical treatments for water pollution reduction
Biological treatments for water pollution reduction
Chemical treatments for water pollution reduction
Treatment of sludge generated in wastewater purification
Domestic Waste: Management, treatment and disposal
Industrial Waste: Management, treatment and disposal
Environmental prevention: IPPC Directive. Environmental impact assessment
Environmental management instruments: Environmental Management Systems, Audits, Life Cycle Analysis
assessment_rules: The final grade for the ordinary call is calculated as 65% for the exam component (either two partials P1 and P2, or a comprehensive final exam E), 12% for Classroom Practicals (PA), 8% for Group Tutorials (TG), and 15% for Laboratory Practicals (PL). Passing requires a minimum of 1.5/5 in exam sub-parts and 4/10 for PA, TG, and PL, with PL also requiring 4/10 in each individual practice; the overall course passing grade is 5/10. The extraordinary call follows a similar weighting but mandates a comprehensive final exam and modifies certain minimum requirements for PA and TG, potentially including a practical exam for PL. Differentiated assessment is 70% for a comprehensive exam, 15% for practical work, and 15% for laboratory practicals, with comparable minimum passing conditions.
